name: Che Fu & The Kratez
venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Che Fu is on a national tour celebrating 25 years since breakthrough album, 'Navigator'. He'll bring his blend of soul, reggae, hip hop, rock, and Pacific influences to the Michael Fowler Centre. He'll be joined on stage by longstanding band The Kratez as well as soul artist Aaradhna, vocalist Betty-Anne, and hip hop artist King Kapisi.

Che Fu appeared on the NZ music scene with funk rockers Supergroove while still in high school. After around five years, he went solo and released hit song 'Chains' in 1996. You might recognise his other chart-topping songs ‘Fade Away’ and ‘Misty Frequencies’ on the 'Navigator' album.

The Niuean/Māori musician became a pioneer of hip-hop and Pasifika music. He was recently inducted into the NZ Music Hall of Fame. He's earned a Pacific Music Awards Lifetime Achievement Award. He's also a Member of the New Zealand Order of Merit.

id: Cornelia Parker-City Gallery Wellington-Wellington NZ
name: Cornelia Parker
venue: City Gallery Wellington
long_description:
After three years of closure, the newly renovated and strengthened City Gallery Wellington Te Whare Toi will host the art of Cornelia Parker. The British visual artist is best known for her innovative and contemporary sculpture and installation art. Her large-scale, immersive installations explore themes of destruction and reconstruction, transformation and metamorphosis. Objects are exploded, crushed, and suspended in a world upended and remade anew.

Curated by independent UK-based curator Andrea Schlieker and City Gallery Wellington’s Senior Curator Aaron Lister, City Gallery Wellington’s exhibition will encompass Parker’s long career as an artist. This includes an immersive sound-and-light installation, ‘Stolen Thunder’. The work gathers the sounds of approaching storms from around the globe and across time. The exhibition will also showcase her paintings, photos, films, and sculptures.

“I have always said this is the one exhibition I want to do before I die,” said Charlotte Davy, Ringatohu Toi Director, Art and City Gallery Wellington. “I have been following Cornelia Parker’s work for the last twenty years. Bringing her mischievous, dark, and literally explosive work to Wellington is incredible.” 

Parker’s work often fills entire rooms and invites the viewer to move through and around the art. Given its physical scale, the blank canvas of the reopened gallery offers the perfect opportunity to host the exhibition. The exhibition will kick off in October 2026 and run through March 2027. 

Charlotte notes the exhibition’s themes are also of particular relevance to Wellington. “I hope that the exhibition and our return to Te Ngākau Civic Square will reflect our city and also help remake it. We are looking forward to opening with a bang.”

Set in a department store, four women meet by chance while shopping for a black lace bra. Though they couldn’t be more different, they quickly discover a shared bond over memory loss, hot flushes, night sweats, and mood swings. What follows is a hilarious, heart-warming musical told with love, laughter and the greatest hits of the 60s, 70s and 80s. The laughter-filled 90-minute production gets audiences out of their seats dancing and singing along to clever parodies of beloved pop classics.

Winner of over 40 Tony Awards, Menopause the Musical has entertained more than 17 million fans worldwide. It’s been translated into nine languages and performed in more than 500 cities. The show’s enduring appeal lies in its honesty, hilarity and heart. It celebrates women everywhere and turns shared experiences into shared joy.

Wellington gets to experience his razor-sharp sense of humour when he visits to promote his latest book - ‘The Land and Its People’. David will take to the stage to read from the collection of essays and freshly minted diary entries. This will be followed by a candid audience Q&A session and an extended book signing that — true to form — will run as long as it needs to.   

In ‘The Land and Its People’ he reflects on what it means to be a foreigner, a brother, and a lifelong friend — trying on the role of caretaker after his partner Hugh’s hip-replacement surgery. Equal parts tender and devastating, it’s classic Sedaris: the kind of writing that makes you laugh until you feel guilty, then laugh again anyway. It has been said that listening to him read is an affirming, joyful experience that leaves a person feeling as if their cup has been filled right to the brim.

In 1988, a group of five rock legends joined together to form The Traveling Wilburys. They were Bob Dylan, George Harrison, Jeff Lynne, Roy Orbison, and Tom Petty. 

Across four years, they produced two mega albums, a slew of hits and won a Grammy. They never toured. Now, a tribute band, The Travelling Wilburys Collective, is on tour and it’s visiting the St James Theatre in Wellington. 

You’ll get to hear some of their biggest and most celebrated hits like Handle with Care, End of the Line, Tweeter and the Monkey Man, and She's My Baby. Along with these original hits, you’ll get served classics from each individual artist and the groups they were in. That includes The Beatles, The Heartbreakers, and ELO. 

The Traveling Wilburys Collection bring together the collective talents, excitement, and magic that the original quintet had to offer. Join them for a night of fun and nostalgia.

id: Richard Dawkins — 50 Years of The Selfish Gene-Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Richard Dawkins — 50 Years of The Selfish Gene
venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Richard Dawkins is a world-renowned evolutionary biologist. When published in 1976, his book, ‘The Selfish Gene’, reframed our understanding of life, behaviour, and human nature. Now, 50 years later, he is coming to Wellington to reflect on the book’s revolutionary legacy. He explores what fifty years of science has confirmed or challenged and explains why its core questions are more urgent today than ever before. 

‘The Selfish Gene’ has remained a cornerstone of modern science. It introduced the gene-centred view of evolution and coined the now-ubiquitous concept of the ‘meme’. The ideas in it ignited global debate and five decades of subsequent research. Richard Dawkins is one of the most consequential scientific communicators of our time, so don’t miss the rare opportunity to hear him speak in person.

venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
By the time indie/folk singer songwriter Aldous Harding hits Wellington, she will have travelled across the UK and Europe with her Train on the Island tour. By the time the tour reaches the Michael Fowler Centre, it will be a finely oiled machine.   

Named after her fifth studio album Train on the Island, all ten of the album’s songs will appear in the concert, including One Stop, and Venus In The Zinnia.   

Aldous Harding captivates listeners with what Martin Pepperell describes as an ‘elastic and shape-shifting voice’. This, combined with eccentric performances, has catapulted the Lyttelton-born singer to fame. Her second album ‘Party’ won the Taite Prize in 2018, and The Barrel, from her third studio album ‘Designer’, won the 2019 APRA Silver Scroll award.

id: Dara Ó Briain: Re:Creation-St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Dara Ó Briain: Re:Creation
venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Having played to sell-out crowds across the UK, Ireland and Northern Europe, Dara Ó Briain is now heading to New Zealand with a new stand-up show. Re:Creation sees one of Ireland’s finest comedians doing his favourite thing — that is, standing in a theatre and captivating an audience with stories. It’s guaranteed to be a very, very funny night. 

Dara has hosted 18 successful series of the comedy panel game Mock the Week for BBC television. In 2012, he was nominated for a BAFTA TV Award for Best Entertainment Performance for his work on the series. He is also a newspaper columnist and has written books for both adults and children. His last tour, ‘So, Where Were We?’ was a huge international success, selling out 173 venues across 20 countries. It was named UK Comedy Tour of the Year 2023 (Chortle).

long_description:
The only ABBA-endorsed tribute show hits Wellington for one spectacular night. Björn Again has been delighting audiences worldwide for over 35 years. They’ve played more than 7,000 shows in over 130 countries to great acclaim. Regarded as the most successful tribute act of all time, members of ABBA have endorsed Björn Again’s outstanding production. Rolling Stone magazine describes them as “fabulously flawless”. Say Gimmie Gimmie Gimmie to the chance to go to a night of 70s Swedish pop nostalgia.

id: Cat Power: The Greatest on Tour-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Cat Power: The Greatest on Tour
venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
20 years on from its release, Cat Power’s album, The Greatest, still retains its mesmeric pull. A late-night classic, it still feels as intimate and raw as it did in 2014. Now you get the chance to hear the album in its entirety live at The Opera House in Wellington.   

The concert won’t just showcase this seminal album — it’ll sit alongside favourite songs from Cat’s catalogue over the past three decades. The concert will drift through heartbreak, survival, longing, and grace with the kind of restraint that only makes the emotional weight hit harder. From the slow-burn sway of Living Proof to the bruised beauty of The Greatest, these songs endure because they tell the truth softly.   

The support act for the Wellington concert is Lawrence Arabia. He is known for his sophisticated songwriting and distinctive blend of indie-pop, chamber-pop and psychedelic influences. Lawrence has toured extensively across New Zealand, Europe and North America.

id: Circa Theatre Season 2026-Circa Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Circa Theatre Season 2026
venue: Circa Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Inside Circa Theatre’s waterfront venue, you’ll find two performance spaces. Both offer a smorgasbord of professional theatre throughout the year. Playwrights from international heavy hitters to brilliant Kiwi voices are represented. It also includes programming from comedies and cabarets to contemporary dance and pantomime. 

Before or after your show, visit the on-site café, brasserie and restaurant, Chouchou. It opens out onto a deck, where you can take in views across the harbour. Look up to admire the art installation above. Called ‘Velarium’, it undulates in the wind, mirroring the water in the harbour. 

Circa Theatre began its life in 1976. A breakaway group of actors and theatre practitioners decided that Aotearoa needed a new and innovative approach to theatre. Five decades later, it is still pushing boundaries, making people laugh and cry, and creating theatrical memories. 

If you don’t have your own Circa memory yet, there’s an opportunity to create one nearly every night of the week.

id: Simple Minds — V Tour-TSB Arena, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Simple Minds — V Tour
venue: TSB Arena, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
One of the world’s most popular and acclaimed live bands, Simple Minds, is heading to Wellington in February. With music styles spanning synth-pop, new wave, and art rock, Simple Minds commanded the stage in the 1980s. The band’s reputation eventually propelled them to stadium-sized gigs, which they filled with anthem-like choruses. Head to the TSB Arena and delve into their enduring catalogue live. You’ll hear global hits like Alive and Kicking, Promised You A Miracle, Waterfront, Don’t You (Forget About Me), Belfast Child, and Sanctify Yourself. It won’t take long before you understand why the band has sold over 60 million albums worldwide. 

The tour includes a very special guest — Gary Numan. Rising to fame with hits like Are ‘Friends’ Electric? and Cars, Gary pioneered a distinctive sound that helped define the future of electronic music in the 80s. His sound has inspired artists across rock, electronic, and alternative music.

id: Chris Parker — Take a Good Hard Look at Me-St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Chris Parker — Take a Good Hard Look at Me
venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
When comedian Chris Parker was young, he liked attention. He’s always endeavoured to make people look at him. In his latest show, he continues the theme of a lifetime. Take a Good Hard Look at Me displays the Kiwi comic’s sharp wit and clever timing. Chris says of his hour-long show — “There’s no secrets about to be dished, no valuable lesson to take away. I’m just a 35-year-old gay man, who was told there was something special about him as a kid and has been grappling with that ever since.” 

Chris is an actor, comedian, writer, and podcaster. He gained fame on TV’s Have You Been Paying Attention and Thank God You’re Here. He has written and performed extensively with Tom Sainsbury on live shows such as The Opening Night Before Christmas, Camping, Giggly Gerties, and Hauraki Horror. He also created and performed several sketch comedy shows with fellow comedian Hayley Sproull, including Tighty Whiteys, The Outsiders’ Guide, and Milky Bits.
